gloss.c.translate.b: A translation app, like Google Translate, helps a lot. You can type, speak, or use conversation mode to talk with a colleague. With the camera you can translate signs, notes and instructions. On many phones, WhatsApp can also translate messages. Use your phone only where it is safe and allowed: not near machines or forklifts, and ask first (more in the lesson "Your phone at work"). Apps make mistakes. For important things, like your contract, a letter or a safety instruction, also ask a person to explain it. Do not take photos of confidential work papers without permission.
gloss.c.translate.p: May I use my phone to translate?
gloss.c.translate.s: Your supervisor gives you a paper with safety instructions in Dutch. You understand only a few words. What do you do?
gloss.c.translate.o1: Ask if you may use a translation app, and ask for an explanation.
gloss.c.translate.o2: Say "ja, ja" and start working. You will understand it later.
gloss.c.translate.o3: Take a photo and send it to a group chat of friends, so they can translate it.
gloss.c.translate.w: A translation app helps you understand quickly, but it can make mistakes. For safety, an explanation from a person is the best check. Work papers can be confidential, so do not share them without permission.
gloss.c.understood.b: Your phone can turn speech into text (live captions): Live Transcribe on Android, Live Captions on iPhone. Check which languages your phone supports. You can also ask someone to write it down, to show it, or to speak slowly. Ask if there is an instruction with pictures, or in your language. Then say back what you understood: "Dus ik moet eerst …?" This is normal here, and it prevents mistakes.
gloss.c.understood.p: So I must count the boxes first?
gloss.c.understood.s: A colleague explains how a new machine works. She speaks fast and you miss some words. What do you do?
gloss.c.understood.o1: Ask her to show it or write it down, and say it back.
gloss.c.understood.o2: Nod and say "ja, ja", so she does not lose time.
gloss.c.understood.o3: Try the machine alone later and see what happens.
gloss.c.understood.w: Showing, writing and saying it back are quick checks. Your colleague can correct you before something goes wrong. Here, this is seen as careful, not as slow.
gloss.c.keeplearning: Keep learning, a little every day
gloss.c.keeplearning.b: A few minutes every day helps more than one long hour a week. Save new words from work in a notes app on your phone. Listen to easy Dutch, for example the NOS Jeugdjournaal (news for children) or a podcast in slow Dutch. Many public libraries have a Taalhuis: free help with Dutch, often with a taalcafé (a place to practise speaking) or a language buddy (taalmaatje). Colleagues often switch to English to help you. Ask them kindly to speak Dutch with you: most people like to help.
gloss.c.keeplearning.p: Just speak Dutch with me, then I learn it faster.
gloss.c.keeplearning.s: Your colleagues always switch to English when they talk to you. You want to learn Dutch. What do you do?
gloss.c.keeplearning.o1: Thank them, and ask them to speak Dutch with you.
gloss.c.keeplearning.o2: Say nothing. Dutch will come by itself.
gloss.c.keeplearning.o3: Answer in English too, because that is more polite.
gloss.c.keeplearning.w: Colleagues often switch to English to be kind. When you ask for Dutch, most of them are happy to help. Speaking a little every day at work is one of the fastest ways to learn.
gloss.c.cv.b: A Dutch CV is short: 1 or 2 pages. Write your contact details, work experience, education, languages and skills. A photo is not needed. You do not have to write your religion, age or marital status. Be honest about what you can do. Ask someone to check your Dutch.
gloss.c.cv.p: Will you read my CV? Is my Dutch correct?
gloss.c.cv.s: You worked 3 years in a factory in your home country, but you have no diploma. What do you put on your CV?
gloss.c.cv.o1: Write the work and what you did there, honestly.
gloss.c.cv.o2: Write nothing, because you have no diploma.
gloss.c.cv.o3: Write that you have a diploma, so you look better.
gloss.c.cv.w: Work experience counts, also from abroad. Being honest is important: employers may check it.
gloss.c.interview.b: Come on time: 5 to 10 minutes early. Greet politely and look at the person. Tell briefly what you can do. Asking questions yourself is normal and positive, for example about the hours, the work or training. At the end you may ask when you will hear something. It is fine to say that you are still learning Dutch. An employer may not ask about your religion, a pregnancy or your health. You do not have to answer: you may politely say that you prefer not to answer.
gloss.c.interview.p: May I ask something too? How many hours per week is the work?
gloss.c.interview.s: At the end of the interview, the employer asks: "Heb je nog vragen?" What do you do?
gloss.c.interview.o1: Ask a question about the hours or training.
gloss.c.interview.o2: Say no, because asking questions is not polite.
gloss.c.interview.o3: Talk more about yourself, to show you are a good worker.
gloss.c.interview.w: Questions show that you are interested in the job. Dutch employers often expect them.
gloss.c.findwork.b: Always ask for a written contract and a copy for yourself. Read it before you sign, or ask someone you trust to help you. A temp agency (uitzendbureau) may not ask you for money to find you a job. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.findwork.p: May I read the contract first?
gloss.c.findwork.s: A new employer says: "Sign here now. You can read it later." What do you do?
gloss.c.findwork.o1: Ask for time to read it, or for a copy.
gloss.c.findwork.o2: Sign quickly, so you do not lose the job.
gloss.c.findwork.o3: Sign, and ask for a copy afterwards.
gloss.c.findwork.w: Your contract says what you earn and what your rights are. A good employer gives you time to read it. You may ask about everything you do not understand.
gloss.c.contract.b: A trial period (proeftijd) must be in writing. It is not allowed in a contract of 6 months or shorter. In a longer contract of less than 2 years, it is at most 1 month. In a contract of 2 years or longer, or a permanent one, it is at most 2 months. On-call worker (oproepkracht)? Your employer must usually call you at least 4 days before. If it is later, you do not have to come. A cao can make these 4 days shorter, but not shorter than 1 day. If they cancel your work later than that, you still get paid. If they call you for less than 3 hours of work, you usually get paid for 3 hours. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.contract.p: Is the trial period in my contract?
gloss.c.contract.s: Your contract is for 3 months. It says: "Proeftijd: 1 maand". What do you do?
gloss.c.contract.o1: Ask about it: this trial period does not count.
gloss.c.contract.o2: Nothing. Every contract has a trial period.
gloss.c.contract.o3: Sign and never ask, because the boss knows best.
gloss.c.contract.w: A trial period in a contract of 6 months or shorter does not count. Asking calmly is normal. If the answer is not clear, get advice from the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.agency.b: If you work through a temp agency (uitzendbureau), the agency is your employer, not the company where you work. Your contract and your pay come from the agency, and there is a cao for temp workers (uitzend-cao). You have a right to the same pay as workers of the company who do the same work. You also get holiday pay (vakantiegeld) and you build up days off. Keep your own list of the hours you worked, and check them on your payslip. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.agency.p: My payslip shows too few hours.
gloss.c.agency.s: Your payslip shows 32 hours, but you worked 38. What do you do?
gloss.c.agency.o1: Show your own list of hours to the agency and ask to fix it.
gloss.c.agency.o2: Say nothing, because it is only 6 hours.
gloss.c.agency.o3: Ask the boss at the company where you work to pay the 6 hours.
gloss.c.agency.w: The agency pays you, so the agency must correct the mistake. Your own list of dates and hours helps. Asking about it is your right.
gloss.c.bsn.b: You get a BSN (burgerservicenummer) when you register at the municipality (gemeente). Here only for a short time? Then you register at an RNI desk. You need your BSN to work, for tax, for health insurance and for a bank account. Your employer needs your ID and your BSN. Do not give your BSN or a copy of your ID to people who do not need it: ask why they need it. Moving? Register your new address at the gemeente within 5 days. DigiD is your login for government websites: never give it to someone else. Do you live or work here? Then you usually must have Dutch health insurance (zorgverzekering). Arrange it quickly. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.bsn.p: Why do you need my BSN?
gloss.c.bsn.s: Someone you do not know offers you a job on WhatsApp. He asks for a photo of your passport and your DigiD login. What do you do?
gloss.c.bsn.o1: Never give your DigiD login. Check who he is first.
gloss.c.bsn.o2: Send everything quickly, so you get the job.
gloss.c.bsn.o3: Send only the passport photo, not your DigiD login.
gloss.c.bsn.w: With your DigiD or a copy of your ID, other people can use your name, for example for loans or benefits. A real employer needs your ID and BSN, but never your DigiD login.
gloss.c.housing.b: Does your employer or agency arrange your housing? Then the rental contract must be separate from your work contract. Ask for a written rental contract and proof of what you pay. Rent may only be taken off your wage if you agreed in writing, and within legal limits: check it on your payslip. A deposit (borg) is at most 2 months of basic rent. You get it back when you leave, minus real damage. Register at your address with the gemeente. Unsafe housing, threats or unfair costs? Report it to the gemeente (meldpunt), and get free advice from the Juridisch Loket or a housing advice service. For a problem with the rent price or service costs, there is the Huurcommissie. Your job ends? Ask for advice before you leave your home. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.housing.p: May I have proof that I paid?
gloss.c.housing.s: Your job ends. The agency says: "You must leave the house tomorrow." What do you do?
gloss.c.housing.o1: Ask the Juridisch Loket for advice first.
gloss.c.housing.o2: Leave right away and forget about your deposit.
gloss.c.housing.o3: Stay, and stop answering the agency.
gloss.c.housing.w: Your rental contract has its own rules, separate from your job. Free advice helps you know your rights, for example about when you must leave and about your deposit.
gloss.c.payslip.b: Bruto is your pay before tax. Netto is what you get in your bank account: bruto minus tax and premiums (loonheffing). Your employer must give you a payslip (loonstrook). Check the hours and the pay on every payslip, and write down the hours you work. Do you have two jobs? Use the tax credit (loonheffingskorting) at only one employer. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.payslip.p: I worked more hours. Can you check it?
gloss.c.payslip.s: Your payslip shows fewer hours than you worked. What do you do?
gloss.c.payslip.o1: Show your notes and ask your supervisor to check it.
gloss.c.payslip.o2: Say nothing, because you do not want problems.
gloss.c.payslip.o3: Wait one month: it will be right on the next payslip.
gloss.c.payslip.w: Mistakes on a payslip happen. Asking about it is normal and it is your right. Your own notes of dates and hours help a lot.
gloss.c.extra.b: You get holiday pay (vakantiegeld): at least 8% of your gross wage. Most employers pay it once a year, in May or June. Your pay may never be lower than the legal minimum wage (minimumloon); for workers under 21 it is lower. The amount changes every year: check it on rijksoverheid.nl. A cao often gives extra pay for overtime or night work. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.extra.p: When do I get my holiday pay?
gloss.c.extra.s: A colleague says: "In May you get extra money from the boss." What is it?
gloss.c.extra.o1: Holiday pay: at least 8% of your gross wage.
gloss.c.extra.o2: A present, only for the best workers.
gloss.c.extra.o3: A 13th month: one extra month of pay, for everyone.
gloss.c.extra.w: Holiday pay is your right, not a gift. You build it up with every hour you work. If you leave your job earlier, you get it with your last pay.
gloss.c.phone.b: Many workplaces do not allow phones during work, especially near machines and forklifts, or in food production. It can be unsafe or not hygienic. Use your phone in your break. Waiting for an urgent call from your family? Tell your supervisor first. Do not take photos or videos at work without permission: think of the privacy of colleagues and company secrets. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.phone.p: My child is sick. May my phone stay on?
gloss.c.phone.s: Your mother is in hospital and may call today. Phones are not allowed on the work floor. What do you do?
gloss.c.phone.o1: Tell your supervisor and ask how you can be reached.
gloss.c.phone.o2: Keep your phone in your pocket and answer quietly at the machine.
gloss.c.phone.o3: Stay home without telling anyone why.
gloss.c.phone.w: Supervisors usually understand a family emergency. When they know, they can find a safe solution, for example a set time to check your phone.
gloss.c.smoking.b: In the Netherlands, smoking inside a workplace is forbidden by law. This is also true for e-cigarettes (vapes). Since 2022, smoking rooms inside companies are not allowed anymore. Smoke only outside, at the place your employer allows, and usually only in your break. Extra smoke breaks are not a right: agree on them with your supervisor. Never smoke near things that burn easily, like fuel or boxes in a warehouse. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.smoking.p: May I smoke outside in my break?
gloss.c.smoking.s: It is cold and raining. A colleague says: "Just smoke in the storage room, nobody sees it." What do you do?
gloss.c.smoking.o1: Say no, and smoke outside at the smoking area in your break.
gloss.c.smoking.o2: Smoke quickly in the storage room, just this once.
gloss.c.smoking.o3: Use your vape inside instead, because that is allowed.
gloss.c.smoking.w: Smoking inside is against the law and can start a fire. A vape inside is not allowed either. Following the rule keeps everyone safe.
gloss.c.clock.b: Clock in and out yourself, at the moment you really start and stop working. Never clock in or out for a colleague, and never let someone else use your card. This counts as fraud and can lead to dismissal. Will you be late? Call before your shift starts. Check that your clocked hours match your payslip. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.clock.p: I forgot to clock out. Can you correct it?
gloss.c.clock.s: A colleague gives you his card: "Clock me in, I will be 20 minutes late." What do you do?
gloss.c.clock.o1: Say no, and tell him to call the supervisor.
gloss.c.clock.o2: Do it just once, because he is your friend.
gloss.c.clock.o3: Clock him in and tell the supervisor later.
gloss.c.clock.w: Clocking in for someone else counts as fraud, for both of you. Saying no protects your colleague and your own job.
gloss.c.hygiene.b: Alcohol and drugs at work, or coming to work after using them, are forbidden in almost all companies. It is very unsafe near machines and forklifts, and it can lead to dismissal. Does a medicine make you sleepy or dizzy? Tell your supervisor, so you can do safe work. You do not have to say which medicine. In food production the hygiene rules are strict: wash your hands, wear clean work clothes, a hairnet if needed, and no jewellery. Vomiting or diarrhoea? Report it before you start. Keep your workplace tidy. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.hygiene.p: I take a medicine. It makes me sleepy.
gloss.c.hygiene.s: Your doctor gives you a medicine that makes you sleepy. Tomorrow you must drive a forklift. What do you do?
gloss.c.hygiene.o1: Tell your supervisor before you start.
gloss.c.hygiene.o2: Say nothing and drive very slowly.
gloss.c.hygiene.o3: Stop taking the medicine without asking your doctor.
gloss.c.hygiene.w: Your supervisor does not need to know which medicine, only that you cannot drive or work with machines now. That keeps you and your colleagues safe.
gloss.c.smalltalk.b: Short chats in the break are normal. They help you feel part of the team. You are welcome at the coffee or lunch table. Easy topics are the weekend, the weather, sports and holidays. Questions about salary, religion or someone’s private life are often too personal at first. On their birthday, people often bring a treat for the team (trakteren), like cake. Is it a colleague’s birthday? Say "Gefeliciteerd!".
gloss.c.smalltalk.s: In the break, your colleagues sit together at a table. You do not know them well yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.smalltalk.o1: Ask "Mag ik bij jullie zitten?" and join with a short chat.
gloss.c.smalltalk.o2: Eat alone outside every day, so you do not disturb them.
gloss.c.smalltalk.o3: Ask each colleague how much they earn.
gloss.c.smalltalk.w: Joining the table is welcome and helps you get to know the team. A simple question like "Hoe was je weekend?" is a good start.
gloss.c.mistakes.b: Everybody makes mistakes at work. Say it quickly, so it can be fixed: "Sorry, ik heb een fout gemaakt." Hiding a mistake is seen as much worse than the mistake itself. Feedback is about the work, not about you as a person. Did you get a compliment? Just say thank you. Not clear what to do better? Ask: "Kun je het uitleggen?"
gloss.c.mistakes.p: Sorry, I made a mistake. How can I fix it?
gloss.c.mistakes.s: You put 20 boxes on the wrong pallet. Nobody has seen it yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.mistakes.o1: Tell your supervisor and help fix it.
gloss.c.mistakes.o2: Say nothing and hope nobody notices.
gloss.c.mistakes.o3: Say that a colleague did it.
gloss.c.mistakes.w: A mistake that is told early is easy to fix. Being honest builds trust, and that counts more than never making a mistake.
gloss.c.respect.b: At work, everyone is equal and everyone is treated with respect, whatever their gender, origin, religion or sexual orientation. You decide about physical contact. A handshake is common, but you may also greet in another polite way, like a nod and a smile, and explain it briefly. Jokes about someone’s origin or religion, threats, bullying (pesten) and unwanted sexual behaviour are not accepted. You can report it to your supervisor, or to a confidential adviser (vertrouwenspersoon) if your company has one.
gloss.c.respect.p: I prefer not to shake hands, but I am happy to greet you.
gloss.c.respect.s: A colleague often makes jokes about your religion. You asked him to stop, but he goes on. What do you do?
gloss.c.respect.o1: Tell your supervisor or the vertrouwenspersoon.
gloss.c.respect.o2: Laugh along, so there is no trouble.
gloss.c.respect.o3: Make jokes about his background back.
gloss.c.respect.w: Such jokes are not accepted at work. Reporting it is normal: the company must keep the workplace safe for everyone.
gloss.c.health.b: The law protects your health. Do you work more than 5.5 hours? Then you get at least 30 minutes of break (it may be 2 times 15 minutes). More than 10 hours? Then at least 45 minutes. A cao can have slightly different break rules. You may work at most 12 hours in one shift and 60 hours in one week. Under 18? Then you may work fewer hours. Your employer must give you protective equipment, like safety shoes or gloves, for free. Unsafe work or too little pay? You can report it to the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie, also without giving your name. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.health.p: I have not had a break yet.
gloss.c.health.s: You have worked 6 hours without a break. Your supervisor asks you to keep going. What do you do?
gloss.c.health.o1: Say that you need your break now.
gloss.c.health.o2: Keep going, and take a longer break later.
gloss.c.health.o3: Leave work and go home without a word.
gloss.c.health.w: When you work more than 5.5 hours, a break is the law, not a favour. Rest also helps you work safely.
gloss.c.rights.b: Discrimination at work is forbidden, for example because of your origin, religion or gender. Your employer cannot simply fire you: normally they need permission from UWV or a judge, or your agreement. (In a trial period or at the end of a temporary contract, other rules apply.) Do not sign a paper about your dismissal that you do not understand. Did you sign an agreement to end your job (vaststellingsovereenkomst)? Then you can usually still cancel it in writing within 14 days. Get help first from the union (for example FNV), a discrimination help desk or the Juridisch Loket (free legal advice). General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.rights.p: I want to ask for advice first.
gloss.c.rights.s: Your boss gives you a paper: "Sign today, then you leave by agreement." You do not understand it well. What do you do?
gloss.c.rights.o1: Do not sign yet. Ask for time and get advice first.
gloss.c.rights.o2: Sign it, because the boss says it is fine.
gloss.c.rights.o3: Put the paper away and never talk about it.
gloss.c.rights.w: If you sign, you can lose rights, for example to unemployment benefit (WW). Asking for time to get advice is normal and allowed.
gloss.c.leave.b: By law you get paid days off: at least 4 times the days you work per week. Full-time, 5 days a week? Then at least 20 days a year. A cao can give more. Ask for leave in time, and in writing. A sudden emergency, like an accident or illness in your family? Then you can get short leave with pay (calamiteitenverlof). Tell your employer right away. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.leave.p: I would like to ask for leave for July.
gloss.c.leave.s: You want to visit your family abroad for three weeks in summer. What do you do?
gloss.c.leave.o1: Ask your employer for leave early, in writing.
gloss.c.leave.o2: Just go, and tell your boss when you are back.
gloss.c.leave.o3: Ask a colleague to tell the boss the day before.
gloss.c.leave.w: Your employer must usually say yes. They may only say no for a very good reason, and then in writing within 2 weeks. Asking early gives the best chance of a yes.
gloss.c.illness: Your rights when you are sick
gloss.c.illness.b: When you are sick, your employer must pay at least 70% of your wage, for up to 2 years. A cao often gives more. There can be up to 2 waiting days (wachtdagen) without pay, but only if your contract or cao says so. Your boss may not ask what illness you have: you talk about your health and your work with the company doctor (bedrijfsarts). Call your employer when you are better (betermelden). In the first year you get at least the minimum wage. A temporary contract stops on its end date, also when you are sick. Working through an agency? If your contract has an agency clause (uitzendbeding), it can end when you get sick. Then ask UWV about the Ziektewet, or ask a union. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.illness.p: I am better again. I will come to work tomorrow.
gloss.c.illness.s: You are sick for a week. Your employer asks you to visit the company doctor. What do you do?
gloss.c.illness.o1: Go, and talk with the doctor about your health and your work.
gloss.c.illness.o2: Do not go, because you already have your own doctor.
gloss.c.illness.o3: Go back to work while you are still sick, so you do not have to go.
gloss.c.illness.w: The company doctor helps you get back to work in a healthy way. The doctor does not tell your boss your medical details, only what work you can do.
gloss.c.warning.b: Watch out for these signs. Your employer keeps your passport or ID: that is not allowed, you keep your own ID and an employer may only make a copy. You get much less pay than agreed, or no payslip. You must pay off a big debt to the employer or agency. You must work extremely long hours, without a choice. Someone threatens you, or uses your housing to put pressure on you. This is not normal and not allowed. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.warning.s: On your first day, the agency says: "We keep your passport, for safety." What do you do?
gloss.c.warning.o1: Keep it yourself. They may make a copy.
gloss.c.warning.o2: Give it, because the agency knows the rules.
gloss.c.warning.o3: Give it, but take a photo of it first.
gloss.c.warning.w: Your passport is yours. Keeping it is a way to control workers. An employer only needs a copy for the files.
gloss.c.gethelp.b: Do you see signs of exploitation, for you or for someone else? Get help. You can report it to the Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie, also anonymously, or to the police. Meld Misdaad Anoniem: 0800-7000. Free legal advice: the Juridisch Loket. In danger? Call 112. Everyone who works in the Netherlands can get help, also migrants. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.gethelp.p: I need help. I am being exploited.
gloss.c.gethelp.s: A friend works 14 hours a day, gets almost no pay and is afraid of the boss. What can you do?
gloss.c.gethelp.o1: Help him contact the Arbeidsinspectie or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.gethelp.o2: Tell him that this is normal for new workers.
gloss.c.gethelp.o3: Tell him to wait until his contract ends, then look for other work.
gloss.c.gethelp.w: Help is there for everyone who works in the Netherlands. A report can also be made without names.
gloss.c.callin.b: When you call your supervisor, say your name, the reason, and when you expect to come back. Sick? You only have to say that you are sick, not what illness you have. Call: do not only send a text, unless your company says a text is fine. No answer? Leave a voice message and try again. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.callin.p: Hello, this is Ali. I cannot come today.
gloss.c.callin.s: Your child is sick and you cannot come to work. Your company wants you to call. What do you do?
gloss.c.callin.o1: Call your supervisor before your shift.
gloss.c.callin.o2: Send a short text at the start of your shift.
gloss.c.callin.o3: Ask your neighbour to call for you.
gloss.c.callin.w: A call is clear and quick, and your supervisor can ask questions. Saying when you expect to be back helps them plan. Also say your name and the reason.
gloss.c.texting: Messages to work: short and polite
gloss.c.texting.b: Keep messages to work short and polite. Say who you are and what is happening, and end with a greeting. For example: "Hoi Mark, ik ben 10 minuten te laat. Sorry! Groet, Ali". Check your roster (rooster) in the app often. Reply to shift requests in time. To swap a shift, your supervisor or the planner must agree first, so ask: "Mag ik mijn dienst ruilen?" Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.texting.p: Hi Mark, I am 10 minutes late. Sorry! Regards, Ali
gloss.c.texting.s: You will be 10 minutes late. Which message to your supervisor is best?
gloss.c.texting.o1: "Hoi Mark, ik ben 10 minuten te laat. Sorry! Groet, Ali"
gloss.c.texting.o2: "Sorry, ik ben er zo!" (without your name, without the time).
gloss.c.texting.o3: A voice message of three minutes about the traffic.
gloss.c.texting.w: A good message says who you are and what is happening, in a few words. Then your supervisor knows it right away.
gloss.c.certs.b: In construction, industry and temp work you often need a VCA certificate (safety). To drive a forklift you usually need a forklift certificate (heftruckcertificaat). Ask your employer if they pay for the course and the exam.
gloss.c.certs.p: Can I do a VCA course here?
gloss.c.certs.s: A job asks for a VCA certificate. You do not have it yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.certs.o1: Ask the employer or agency to help you get it.
gloss.c.certs.o2: Do not apply, because you will never get the job.
gloss.c.certs.o3: Say you have it, and hope nobody checks.
gloss.c.certs.w: Many employers and agencies help with VCA. Asking shows that you want to learn.
gloss.c.diploma.b: Do you have a diploma from another country? You can have it assessed at IDW (Internationale Diplomawaardering). Then employers can see what it is worth here. Is a training required for your job? Then your employer must pay for it, and it counts as working time. Ask your supervisor about courses. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.diploma.s: Your employer says you must do a required safety training on Saturday, without pay. What is true?
gloss.c.diploma.o1: The employer pays it, and it is working time.
gloss.c.diploma.o2: Training is always in your own free time.
gloss.c.diploma.o3: You must pay for the training yourself.
gloss.c.diploma.w: If a training is required for your work, the employer pays and it counts as working time. If it is not clear, ask for advice.
gloss.c.doctor.b: Register with a family doctor (huisarts) near your home. Do you need urgent care in the evening, at night or in the weekend? Call the huisartsenpost. Call 112 only in an emergency: danger to life, fire, or a crime happening now. You get medicines at the pharmacy (apotheek).
gloss.c.doctor.p: I want to register with the GP.
gloss.c.doctor.s: It is Saturday night. Your child has a high fever, but is awake and breathing normally. What do you do?
gloss.c.doctor.o3: Wait until Monday and do nothing.
gloss.c.doctor.w: The huisartsenpost helps with urgent care outside office hours. 112 is for emergencies: danger to life, fire, or a crime happening now.
gloss.c.insurance.b: When you live or work in the Netherlands, basic health insurance is usually required. You pay a premium every month. Every year there is an own risk (eigen risico): the first costs you pay yourself. The amount changes: check it with your insurer. Visits to the family doctor (huisarts) do not count for the own risk. With a low income you may get healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag). General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.insurance.p: I need health insurance. Can you help me?
gloss.c.insurance.s: You started working here two weeks ago and you have no health insurance yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.insurance.o2: Wait: your insurance from home is enough.
gloss.c.insurance.o3: Use the insurance card of a friend.
gloss.c.insurance.w: Without insurance, a doctor or hospital can cost a lot, and you can get a fine. Arranging it quickly protects you. Your employer or agency can help you.
gloss.c.letters.b: Do not ignore letters from the Belastingdienst, the gemeente or UWV. Ask someone you trust to help you read them. The tax return (aangifte) for last year must usually be done before 1 May. You can ask for more time. Allowances (toeslagen) like zorgtoeslag and huurtoeslag depend on your income. If you get too much, you must pay it back, so keep your income details up to date. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.letters.p: I got a letter. Can you help me?
gloss.c.letters.s: You get a letter from the Belastingdienst. You do not understand it. What do you do?
gloss.c.letters.o1: Ask someone you trust to help you read it.
gloss.c.letters.o2: Put it in a drawer and wait.
gloss.c.letters.o3: Throw it away, because it is probably advertising.
gloss.c.letters.w: Official letters often have a deadline. If you react in time, problems are usually easier to solve.
gloss.c.scams.b: Your bank never asks for your codes or PIN by phone, SMS or email. Do not click on links in messages you did not expect. Someone pressures you to pay fast? Stop and check first. Call your bank on the official number, for example the number on your bank card or its website.
gloss.c.scams.p: I will call the bank back myself.
gloss.c.scams.s: You get an SMS: "Your bank account will be blocked. Click this link now." What do you do?
gloss.c.scams.o1: Do not click. Call your bank on the official number.
gloss.c.scams.o2: Click quickly, so your account is not blocked.
gloss.c.scams.o3: Reply to the SMS and ask if it is real.
gloss.c.scams.w: Scammers use pressure and fake links. Your bank never asks for your codes through a link or a message.
gloss.c.bike.b: Turn your lights on when it is dark. Ride on the bike path and follow the traffic lights and signs. Always lock your bike. Holding your phone in your hand while cycling is forbidden.
gloss.c.bike.p: Where can I park my bike?
gloss.c.bike.s: It is dark and you cycle to your night shift. Your phone rings. What do you do?
gloss.c.bike.o1: Stop at a safe place before you answer.
gloss.c.bike.o2: Answer with the phone in your hand while cycling.
gloss.c.bike.o3: Ride on, and look at your phone quickly.
gloss.c.bike.w: A phone in your hand while cycling is forbidden and dangerous. Stopping first takes only a moment.
gloss.c.transit.b: In most buses and trains you can pay with your bank card (OVpay). Check in AND check out with the same card, or you pay too much. A travel allowance (reiskostenvergoeding) is not a legal right: it depends on your employer or cao. Ask about it. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.transit.p: Do I get money for my travel costs?
gloss.c.transit.s: You travel to work by bus every day. A colleague gets travel money, you do not. What do you do?
gloss.c.transit.o1: Ask your supervisor about the company or cao rules.
gloss.c.transit.o2: Say nothing, because it is probably not for you.
gloss.c.transit.o3: Tell your supervisor: the law says you must get it too.
gloss.c.transit.w: Travel allowance depends on the employer or the cao. Asking about it is normal and helps you know your rights.
gloss.c.ww.b: Lost your job? Apply for WW at UWV as soon as possible, within a week after your first day without work. You usually need to have worked at least 26 of the last 36 weeks. If you quit your job yourself, you usually do not get WW. Register as a job seeker on werk.nl. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.ww.p: I want to apply for unemployment benefit. What must I do?
gloss.c.ww.s: You are angry about your work and want to quit today. What is wise?
gloss.c.ww.o1: Get advice first, before you quit.
gloss.c.ww.o2: Quit today: you will get WW anyway.
gloss.c.ww.o3: Stop coming to work without saying anything.
gloss.c.ww.w: Quitting can cost you your benefit. Talking first with your supervisor, the union or the Juridisch Loket can help you find a better way.
gloss.c.newjob.b: Before you leave, ask for a reference (referentie). Keep your payslips and your contract. Update your CV. Look for work at temp agencies (uitzendbureaus) and on werk.nl. Never pay money to get a job. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.newjob.p: May I give your name as a reference?
gloss.c.newjob.s: Someone offers you a job, but first you must pay 300 euros "for the job". What do you do?
gloss.c.newjob.o1: Do not pay. Look for a real agency.
gloss.c.newjob.o2: Pay, because a good job is worth it.
gloss.c.newjob.o3: Pay half now and the rest later.
gloss.c.newjob.w: Asking money for a job is a warning sign. A temp agency may not charge you for finding work. You can also look for work on werk.nl.
gloss.c.tools.b: On many building sites there is a short safety meeting at regular times: the toolbox meeting. You hear about risks and new rules. Go to it, listen, and ask questions if you do not understand. Check your tools before you use them. Is a tool broken? Tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.tools.p: This drill is broken. Is there another one?
gloss.c.tools.s: There is a toolbox meeting, but your Dutch is not good yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.tools.o1: Go, and ask a colleague afterwards what you missed.
gloss.c.tools.o2: Skip it, because you will not understand it anyway.
gloss.c.tools.o3: Sign the attendance list without going.
gloss.c.tools.w: Safety information is for everyone. A translation app can help you follow the meeting, if phones are allowed there. Asking a colleague afterwards is normal and checks that you understood it right.
gloss.c.site.b: Before you start a job, stop for a moment and check: what can go wrong here? This is the LMRA (last-minute risk analysis). Always wear your helmet, and fall protection when you work high. Never stand under a hanging load. Is the work really dangerous? Then you may stop, and you must tell your supervisor right away. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.site.p: I am not starting yet. This is not safe.
gloss.c.site.s: You must work on a scaffold, but a railing is missing. A colleague says: "Just be careful." What do you do?
gloss.c.site.o1: Do not start. Report it to your supervisor first.
gloss.c.site.o3: Fix the railing yourself with some rope.
gloss.c.site.w: A fall from height can cause very serious injuries. You may stop dangerous work, and reporting it protects the whole team.
gloss.c.line.b: Never reach into a running machine, not even for a second. At a fault (storing): press the emergency stop (noodstop) and call your supervisor. Maintenance and repairs are done only when the machine is locked off (lock-out), and only by trained people. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.line.p: There is a fault. I pressed the emergency stop.
gloss.c.line.s: A product is stuck in the machine. The machine is still running. What do you do?
gloss.c.line.o1: Press the emergency stop and call your supervisor.
gloss.c.line.o2: Quickly pull it out with your hand.
gloss.c.line.o3: Leave it and hope the machine fixes it.
gloss.c.line.w: Running machines can cause serious accidents in a second. Stopping the machine is always allowed and always better.
gloss.c.quality.b: Do you see a problem with a product, like damage or a wrong label? Report it and put it aside. Do not let it pass just to keep the line going. Finding a problem early saves a lot of work and money. Your supervisor will be glad you said it.
gloss.c.quality.p: I think something is wrong with these products.
gloss.c.quality.s: You see that many products have a wrong date on the label. The line is very busy. What do you do?
gloss.c.quality.o1: Tell your supervisor or the quality person right away.
gloss.c.quality.o2: Let them pass, because it is not your job.
gloss.c.quality.w: A wrong label can mean that all products must come back from the shops. Saying it early is what a good team member does.
gloss.c.client.b: Knock before you go into a client’s room. Say who you are, explain what you are going to do and ask permission. Say "u" to clients, unless they ask you to say "je". Let clients do what they can do themselves.
gloss.c.client.p: May I come in? I am here to help you wash.
gloss.c.client.s: You must help a client to wash. The door of her room is closed. What do you do?
gloss.c.client.o1: Knock, wait, and say who you are and why.
gloss.c.client.o2: Walk in quickly, because you are busy.
gloss.c.client.o3: Skip the washing, so you do not disturb her.
gloss.c.client.w: The room is the client’s home. Knocking and explaining shows respect and makes the care calmer.
gloss.c.privacy.b: What you see and hear about clients stays at work. Do not talk about clients outside work, and never post photos of them. Clean your hands before and after care. Do you notice a change in a client, like pain or a fall? Tell the nurse right away. Never give medicines unless you are trained and allowed to do it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.privacy.p: The man has more pain than yesterday.
gloss.c.privacy.s: A client asks you for her pills. You are not trained to give medicines. What do you do?
gloss.c.privacy.o1: Say kindly that you will get the nurse.
gloss.c.privacy.o2: Give the pills, because she knows what she needs.
gloss.c.privacy.w: Wrong medicine can be dangerous. Getting the right person quickly helps the client and keeps everyone safe.
gloss.c.kitchen.b: Wash your hands often, also after the toilet and after touching raw meat. Keep cold food cold and hot food hot. Put a label with the date on food you store. These rules are called HACCP. Allergies are serious: not sure what is in a dish? Always ask the chef. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.kitchen.p: Chef, is there gluten in this sauce?
gloss.c.kitchen.s: A guest asks if a dish has nuts in it. You are not sure. What do you do?
gloss.c.kitchen.o1: Say you will check, and ask the chef.
gloss.c.kitchen.o2: Say "no", so the guest is happy.
gloss.c.kitchen.o3: Tell the guest to pick out the nuts.
gloss.c.kitchen.w: For a guest with an allergy, a small mistake can be very dangerous. Checking with the chef is always right.
gloss.c.service.b: Say "u" to guests, unless they ask you to say "je". Be friendly and calm, also when it is busy. Not sure about a question? Say that you will check. Tips (fooi): the rules differ per place. Ask how tips are shared where you work.
gloss.c.service.p: One moment, I will be with you soon.
gloss.c.service.s: It is very busy. A guest calls you, but you are carrying plates to another table. What do you do?
gloss.c.service.o1: Look at the guest and say: "Een moment, ik kom zo bij u."
gloss.c.service.o2: Ignore the guest until you have time.
gloss.c.service.o3: Put the plates down on a free table and go to the guest first.
gloss.c.service.w: A short sign shows the guest that you saw them. Then you can finish your task calmly.
gloss.c.cleaning.b: Every cleaning product has a label. Pictograms (small pictures in a red diamond) show the danger, for example for your skin, eyes or lungs. Read the label, or ask what the product is for and how to use it. Wear the gloves your employer gives you. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.cleaning.s: You get a new cleaning product. You cannot read the label well. What do you do?
gloss.c.cleaning.o1: Ask how you can use it safely.
gloss.c.cleaning.o2: Use a lot of it, then it works better.
gloss.c.cleaning.w: The wrong product, or too much of it, can hurt your skin, eyes or lungs. Asking takes one minute.
gloss.c.cleansafe.b: Never mix cleaning products, for example bleach and a toilet cleaner. This can make dangerous gases. Let fresh air in. Mopping a floor? Put down the wet-floor sign (Pas op, glad!), so nobody slips. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.cleansafe.p: I am putting the sign down. The floor is wet.
gloss.c.cleansafe.s: The toilet is very dirty. A colleague says: "Mix two products, then it works better." What do you do?
gloss.c.cleansafe.o1: Do not mix them. Use one product.
gloss.c.cleansafe.o2: Mix them, but open a window.
gloss.c.cleansafe.o3: Mix them quickly and leave the room.
gloss.c.cleansafe.w: Mixing products can make poisonous gas, even with a window open. One product, used well, is enough.
gloss.s.gossip.1: I do not gossip about colleagues.
gloss.s.gossip.2: I do not put photos of work online.
gloss.s.gossip.3: I would rather you say it to me.
gloss.c.gossip.q: Did you hear what Mark did?
gloss.c.gossip.a: No, and I would rather not talk about him.
gloss.s.boundaries.2: I do not find that remark funny.
gloss.s.boundaries.3: I want to report something to the confidential adviser.
gloss.c.boundaries.q: Do not be so difficult, it was only a joke.
gloss.c.boundaries.a: Not for me. I want you to stop.
gloss.c.gossip.b: Talking behind a colleague’s back (roddelen) harms the trust in a team. Do you have a problem with someone? Talk to that person, or to your supervisor. Online, the same rules apply as at work: do not post photos, videos or messages about colleagues, clients or the company without permission. Your boss can see what you post, and it can stay online for years. Many teams have a group chat (groepsapp) for work: keep it about work, and do not share screenshots of it with others. Sharing private things of a colleague or mocking someone online is bullying too.
gloss.c.gossip.p: I do not want that online.
gloss.c.gossip.s: A colleague films you when you slip on the wet floor. He wants to put the video on TikTok. What do you do?
gloss.c.gossip.o1: Say "Nee, dat wil ik niet" and ask him to delete it.
gloss.c.gossip.o2: Laugh and let him post it, so you are not difficult.
gloss.c.gossip.o3: Ask him to post it without your name.
gloss.c.gossip.w: Nobody may put a video of you online without your permission. Saying no is normal, and your employer must act when colleagues mock each other online. If he posts it anyway, tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.boundaries.b: Grensoverschrijdend gedrag is behaviour that crosses someone’s boundary: unwanted touching, sexual remarks or jokes, staring, sending unwanted pictures, threats or shouting. It does not matter if the other person "meant it as a joke": what counts is how it feels to you. If you can, say clearly that you want it to stop. Write down what happened, when, and who saw it. Tell your supervisor, the confidential adviser (vertrouwenspersoon, if there is one) or HR. Your employer must protect you, and you may not be punished for reporting it. Did you see it happen to a colleague? Ask if they are okay, and offer to be a witness.
gloss.c.boundaries.s: Your team leader often puts his hand on your back and says you look "pretty". It makes you feel uncomfortable. He decides your shifts. What do you do?
gloss.c.boundaries.o1: Write it down and tell the vertrouwenspersoon.
gloss.c.boundaries.o2: Say nothing, because he decides your shifts.
gloss.c.boundaries.o3: Quit your job without telling anyone why.
gloss.c.boundaries.w: This is unwanted behaviour, and it is not your fault. A confidential adviser listens in confidence and helps you choose the next step. You are protected when you report it. You can also talk to HR.
gloss.s.shelves.1: Put the new products at the back.
gloss.s.shelves.2: This product is past its date.
gloss.c.shelves.q: Where can I find the rice?
gloss.c.shelves.a: In aisle four. I will walk there with you.
gloss.s.checkout.1: Would you like to pay by card or in cash?
gloss.s.checkout.3: May I see your ID, please?
gloss.c.checkout.q: Can I pay by card here?
gloss.w.kwartier: a quarter of an hour (15 minutes)
gloss.s.hours.1: I start at half past seven (7:30).
gloss.s.hours.3: The break lasts half an hour.
gloss.c.shelves.b: When you stock the shelves, look at the date on the products. Put the products with the soonest date at the front, and the new ones at the back. Customers take from the front, so the old products go first. Is a product past its date, or damaged? Take it off the shelf and ask what to do with it. Keep the aisles free of boxes and carts. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shelves.p: What do I do with products past their date?
gloss.c.shelves.s: You are putting new milk on the shelf. At the front there is still milk with a sooner date. What do you do?
gloss.c.shelves.o1: Put the new milk at the back, and the old milk at the front.
gloss.c.shelves.o2: Put the new milk at the front, because it is fresher.
gloss.c.shelves.o3: Throw the old milk away, so the shelf looks nice.
gloss.c.shelves.w: Customers take from the front. When the old products go first, less food is thrown away.
gloss.c.checkout.b: You may not sell alcohol or tobacco to anyone under 18: this is the law. Not sure how old a customer is? Ask for their ID. Many shops ask for ID from everyone who looks younger than 25. No ID, or under 18? Then you do not sell it, and you stay polite. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.checkout.p: Without ID I may not sell this.
gloss.c.checkout.s: A young man wants to buy beer. He looks about 17. He says he is 19, but he has no ID with him. What do you do?
gloss.c.checkout.o1: Say you cannot sell it without ID.
gloss.c.checkout.o2: Sell it, because he says he is 19.
gloss.c.checkout.o3: Sell it, but only one can.
gloss.c.checkout.w: Without ID you cannot know his age. Selling alcohol to someone under 18 is against the law, and the shop can get a fine.
gloss.c.hours.b: In Dutch, "half" counts to the next hour: half acht is 7:30, not 8:30. Kwart over acht is 8:15, and kwart voor acht is 7:45. Check your hours yourself: the end time minus the start time, minus the break. A break is often not paid. Write down your hours every day.
gloss.c.hours.p: Half acht? So half an hour before eight?
gloss.c.hours.s: Your supervisor says: "Morgen begin je om half negen." What time do you start tomorrow?
gloss.c.hours.w: "Half negen" means half an hour before nine: 8:30. Many newcomers think it is 9:30, and come an hour late.
gloss.c.measures: Count smart, measure, do not guess
gloss.c.measures.b: Many boxes to count? Count the boxes in one layer, and the number of layers. Then multiply: 8 boxes in a layer and 5 layers is 40 boxes. With cleaning products, measure the amount the label says. More is not better: it can hurt your skin and costs money. Not sure about a number? Count again, or ask. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.measures.s: A pallet has 6 layers. Each layer has 8 boxes. Your supervisor asks how many boxes there are. What do you say?
gloss.c.measures.w: 6 layers of 8 boxes is 6 times 8: 48. Counting one layer and multiplying is quick, and a real number is better than a guess.
gloss.w.chatbot: the chatbot (an app you can chat with)
gloss.w.meekijken: to look at it together with someone
gloss.w.kloppen: to be right, to be correct
gloss.s.aihelp.3: Could you have a look with me?
gloss.w.gegevens: the details, the data (name, address, number)
gloss.s.aiprivate.1: I do not share names of customers.
gloss.s.aiprivate.2: May I use AI for my work?
gloss.c.aiprivate.q: Just put this in the chatbot.
gloss.c.aiprivate.a: I would rather not, it has names of customers in it.
gloss.s.aifake.2: I hang up and call back myself.
gloss.c.aifake.q: Hi, this is my new number. Can you quickly send money?
gloss.c.aifake.a: First I will call you on your old number.
gloss.s.aiplan.2: I want to talk to a person.
gloss.s.aiplan.3: Why do I have fewer hours in my schedule?
gloss.c.aiplan.a: Can I talk to a person about it?
gloss.c.aihelp.b: AI apps and chatbots, like ChatGPT, can translate, explain a letter or help you write a message. That is useful. But AI sometimes makes mistakes, and still sounds very sure. For important things, like your contract, your pay, medicine or safety, always check the answer with a person: your supervisor, HR or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.aihelp.p: Is this right? Could you have a look with me?
gloss.c.aihelp.s: You ask a chatbot about your contract. It says you get no holiday pay. What do you do?
gloss.c.aihelp.o1: Ask HR or the Juridisch Loket to check it.
gloss.c.aihelp.o2: Believe it: the chatbot sounds very sure.
gloss.c.aihelp.o3: Say nothing and forget about it.
gloss.c.aihelp.w: A chatbot can be wrong about rules and contracts. In the Netherlands almost every worker gets holiday pay. A person who knows the rules can check it.
gloss.c.aiprivate.b: What you type into a chatbot can be saved and used by the company that makes it. So never type your BSN, a password or your bank details. Do not put in names or photos of customers, patients or colleagues, or papers from work. Many employers have rules about AI. Ask first if you may use it for your work. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.aiprivate.p: May I use AI for this?
gloss.c.aiprivate.s: You want a chatbot to write a report about a customer. The report has the name and address of the customer. What do you do?
gloss.c.aiprivate.o1: Ask first, and leave the name and address out.
gloss.c.aiprivate.o2: Put everything in the chatbot: it is faster.
gloss.c.aiprivate.o3: Send the report to a friend to check it.
gloss.c.aiprivate.w: Names and addresses are personal data. They may not just go to another company. Your employer knows which apps are allowed.
gloss.c.aifake.b: With AI, criminals can copy a voice and make fake photos and videos. A call or message that sounds like your boss, your bank or someone in your family can be fake. Be careful when there is haste, money and a new number. Hang up, and call back yourself on the number you know. A real bank, employer or the police never asks for your codes.
gloss.c.aifake.p: I hang up and call back myself.
gloss.c.aifake.s: Your phone rings. A voice that sounds just like your boss says: "Pay this bill now, it is urgent." What do you do?
gloss.c.aifake.o1: Hang up and call your boss back yourself.
gloss.c.aifake.o2: Pay quickly: it is your boss.
gloss.c.aifake.o3: Give your bank code, so your boss can pay it.
gloss.c.aifake.w: A voice can be copied with AI. Haste and money together are a warning sign. Calling back on a number you know is a quick and safe check.
gloss.c.aiplan.b: More and more companies let an app or a computer make the roster, count your speed with the scanner, or decide things. You may ask which information about you is collected. Is there a big decision about you, like fewer hours, a warning or dismissal? Ask who decided it. When a computer made such a decision on its own, you may ask a person to look at it again and explain it. Write down your own hours. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.aiplan.p: Can a person have a look at this?
gloss.c.aiplan.s: The planning app gives you far fewer hours next month. Nobody tells you why. What do you do?
gloss.c.aiplan.o1: Ask a person to explain it.
gloss.c.aiplan.o2: Accept it: the app is always right.
gloss.c.aiplan.o3: Ask the chatbot in the app why.
gloss.c.aiplan.w: Apps make mistakes, and they do not know everything about you. You may ask for an explanation, and a person can look at it again.
gloss.s.harvest.2: Which row do I start in?
gloss.c.harvest.q: How many rows have you done?
gloss.w.hitte: the heat (when it is very hot)
gloss.s.greensafe.2: I am going to drink some water.
gloss.c.greensafe.q: May I work in greenhouse three?
gloss.c.greensafe.a: No, not yet. It was just sprayed.
gloss.c.harvest.b: In a greenhouse you often work at a set pace (tempo). Some employers pay per crate, per row or per kilo: piece rate (stukloon). Even with piece rate, you must earn at least the minimum wage for every hour you work. Check the amount on rijksoverheid.nl. Write down your hours and your crates every day, and compare them with your payslip. Working fast is good, but working safely comes first. General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.harvest.p: How many crates did I do today?
gloss.c.harvest.s: You are paid per crate. At the end of the week, your pay is much lower than the minimum wage for the hours you worked. What do you do?
gloss.c.harvest.o1: Show your employer your own list of hours and crates.
gloss.c.harvest.o2: Say nothing and work faster next week, so you earn more.
gloss.c.harvest.o3: Accept it: with piece rate, a low pay is normal.
gloss.c.harvest.w: With piece rate you must still get at least the minimum wage for every hour you worked. Your own list of hours and crates helps you show what you did. If it is not fixed, ask for help.
gloss.c.greensafe.b: In a greenhouse it can get very hot, also in spring. Drink water often, also before you feel thirsty, and take your breaks in a cool place. Do you feel dizzy or sick, or do you get a headache? Stop and tell someone. Plants are sometimes sprayed with chemicals (spuitmiddelen). A greenhouse that was just sprayed often has a sign at the door. Do not go in until your supervisor says it is safe again. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.greensafe.p: May I already work in this greenhouse?
gloss.c.greensafe.s: A greenhouse was sprayed this morning. There is a sign on the door. A colleague says: "Come on, it is only for a moment." What do you do?
gloss.c.greensafe.o1: Stay outside and ask when it is safe.
gloss.c.greensafe.o2: Go in quickly and hold your breath.
gloss.c.greensafe.o3: Go in, and wash your hands well afterwards.
gloss.c.greensafe.w: Crop sprays can hurt your skin, eyes and lungs, also when you smell nothing. After spraying there is a waiting time before people may go in again. Your supervisor knows when it is over.

gloss.s.jobends.2: I ask for advice at the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.s.jobends.3: I arrange new health insurance myself.
gloss.c.jobends.q: Your work ends on Friday. Then you must leave the house too.
gloss.c.jobends.a: What is the notice period of my rental contract?
gloss.c.details.b: At the start of a job, you give your details: your name, address, phone number, date of birth and BSN. Spell your name slowly, letter by letter. Then check your name on your contract and your payslip. A mistake in your name or BSN can give problems with your pay or tax. New address or phone number? Tell your employer.
gloss.c.details.p: Let me spell it: A, L, I.
gloss.c.details.s: On the phone, the agency writes down your last name. You hear that they write it wrong. What do you do?
gloss.c.details.o1: Spell your name slowly and ask them to read it back.
gloss.c.details.o2: Say nothing: a small mistake in your name does not matter.
gloss.c.details.o3: Hang up, and hope they find the mistake later.
gloss.c.details.w: Your name must be the same on your contract, your payslip and your ID. Then your pay and your tax go right. Spelling and reading back is a quick check.
gloss.c.dates.b: In Dutch, the day comes before the month: 3-6 is 3 June, not 6 March. "Tot en met" means that the last day counts too. Days and months start with a small letter: maandag, juni. Not sure about a date? Ask, and say it back.
gloss.c.dates.s: Your roster says: "Vrij: 3-6 tot en met 5-6". When are you free?
gloss.c.dates.w: The day comes first, then the month: 3-6 is 3 June. "Tot en met" means that 5 June counts too, so you are free for three days.
gloss.c.permit.b: Do you have to do the civic integration (inburgering)? Tell your employer, and tell the gemeente that you work. Ask early if your language classes can fit around your roster. Not sure if you may work here? Check it before you start, for example at the IND, UWV or VluchtelingenWerk. Do they ask you to register as self-employed (zzp’er) for this job? Ask for advice first. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.permit.p: I have a language class on Tuesday. Can my roster take that into account?
gloss.c.permit.s: You start a new job. Your language class is on Tuesday mornings, but your roster has you working on Tuesdays. What do you do?
gloss.c.permit.o1: Tell your supervisor and ask to change the roster.
gloss.c.permit.o2: Skip the language class, because work comes first.
gloss.c.permit.o3: Stay home on Tuesdays without saying anything.
gloss.c.permit.w: Your integration is a duty too. Many employers help when they know it early. The gemeente can also help you fit your plan around your work.
gloss.c.kids.b: Is your child suddenly sick? Tell your employer right away. For the first hours or days you can take emergency leave (calamiteitenverlof), and your employer keeps paying you. Does your child need care for longer? Then you can ask for care leave (zorgverlof). Pregnant? Your employer may not fire you because of that. Ask in time about pregnancy leave and parental leave (ouderschapsverlof). General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.kids.p: My child is sick. Can I leave early today?
gloss.c.kids.s: The daycare (kinderopvang) calls you at work. Your child has a fever and must go home. What do you do?
gloss.c.kids.o1: Tell your supervisor, and ask for emergency leave.
gloss.c.kids.o2: Leave without a word, and explain it tomorrow.
gloss.c.kids.o3: Stay at work, and let your child wait until your shift ends.
gloss.c.kids.w: A sick child is an emergency at home. When you tell your supervisor first, they can plan the work. Emergency leave is for moments like this.
gloss.c.body: Say what happened and where it hurts
gloss.c.body.b: At the doctor, say what happened and where it hurts. For example: "Ik ben gevallen. Mijn arm doet pijn." Also say how long you have had the pain. You do not have to guess what you have: the doctor checks that. Did it happen at work? Tell your supervisor the same day.
gloss.c.body.s: You lifted a heavy box at work. Now your back hurts a lot. You are at the family doctor (huisarts). What do you say?
gloss.c.body.o1: Where it hurts, and what happened: you lifted a heavy box.
gloss.c.body.o2: Only that you feel bad, nothing more.
gloss.c.body.o3: The name of an illness you found on the internet.
gloss.c.body.w: When you say where it hurts and what happened, the doctor understands you faster. The doctor checks what it is. Did it happen at work? Tell your supervisor too.
gloss.c.jobends: Your job ends: what else stops?
gloss.c.jobends.b: When your job ends, check your final pay (eindafrekening). Days off you did not use and your holiday pay are usually paid out with it. Housing, health insurance or a van through the agency can stop at the same time. Arrange your own health insurance in time. Your rental contract has its own rules: ask for advice before you leave the house. Moving, or leaving the Netherlands? Tell the gemeente. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.jobends.p: When do I get my final pay?
gloss.c.jobends.s: Your job ends on Friday. Your health insurance goes through the agency. What do you do?
gloss.c.jobends.o1: Ask when it stops and arrange your own in time.
gloss.c.jobends.o2: Nothing: the insurance goes on by itself.
gloss.c.jobends.o3: Wait until you get sick, and arrange it then.
gloss.c.jobends.w: Insurance through the agency often stops when your job stops. When you live or work in the Netherlands, you usually must have health insurance. Arranging it in time keeps you covered.

gloss.c.healthy.q: Do you want a pill? Then you stay awake.
gloss.c.healthy.a: No, thank you. I do not work under the influence.
gloss.c.workorder.b: Before you start, read the work order (werkbon) or the task in the app. Check the address, the task and the number of things. Something is not clear? Ask before you start, not halfway. Then put your tools and materials ready. That saves time, and you make fewer mistakes. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.workorder.p: The work order says ten boxes. Is that right?
gloss.c.workorder.s: Your work order says: paint room 3. Your colleague says it is room 5. What do you do?
gloss.c.workorder.o1: Ask your supervisor which room is right.
gloss.c.workorder.o2: Paint room 3, because the work order says so.
gloss.c.workorder.o3: Paint both rooms, then you are sure.
gloss.c.workorder.w: When two things do not match, you check before you start. A short question costs less time than doing the work again.
gloss.c.handover: Say what is done, and what is not
gloss.c.handover.b: Your work is not done when you stop. First tidy up your place and your tools. Then ask someone to check your work. Tell your supervisor what is done and what is not done. Did something go wrong, or is something broken? Say it now, not tomorrow. Signing off is part of your work. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.handover.p: Room four is not done yet. The door was locked.
gloss.c.handover.s: You cleaned five rooms. Room 4 was locked, so you could not clean it. Your shift ends. What do you do?
gloss.c.handover.o1: Tell your supervisor that room 4 is not done, and why.
gloss.c.handover.o2: Go home: room 4 was locked, so it is not your fault.
gloss.c.handover.o3: Write "all done" on the list, because you did your best.
gloss.c.handover.w: Your supervisor plans the work. When they know that room 4 is not done, they can send someone else. Then no customer finds a dirty room.
gloss.c.workshop.b: Grinding, sawing and drilling make sparks, small bits and a lot of noise. Wear safety glasses and hearing protection, also for a short job. When it is very loud, your employer must give you hearing protection. Sparks can start a fire. For welding, or grinding near things that can burn, there are extra rules (heet werk): ask before you start. After your work, clean up the bits of metal. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.workshop.p: I am going to grind. Where is the hearing protection?
gloss.c.workshop.s: You must grind one small piece of metal. It takes one minute. Your safety glasses are in the other room. What do you do?
gloss.c.workshop.o1: Get your glasses first, also for one minute.
gloss.c.workshop.o2: Grind with your eyes half closed, it is quick.
gloss.c.workshop.o3: Hold your other hand in front of your eyes.
gloss.c.workshop.w: A spark or a bit of metal in your eye can hurt your eye for good. That can happen in one second. Safety glasses help, also for a short job.
gloss.c.power.b: Never work on something that has power on it (onder spanning). First a trained colleague makes it safe: they switch off the power and check it. Only people with the right training may do this. Do you see a broken cable or plug? Do not use it, and tell your supervisor right away. Not sure if the power is off? Then it is on. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.power.p: I see a broken cable. Who can look at it?
gloss.c.power.s: You must hang a lamp. A colleague says: "The power is off, I think." What do you do?
gloss.c.power.o1: Ask a trained colleague to check that the power is off.
gloss.c.power.o2: Start, but wear thick gloves when you touch the wires.
gloss.c.power.o3: Switch the light on and off to check that the power is off.
gloss.c.power.w: "I think" is not enough with electricity. A shock can kill you. A trained colleague checks that there is no power, and then you can start.
gloss.c.garage.b: Never go under a car that only stands on a jack. The car must stand firmly on the lift or on stands. Spilled oil makes the floor slippery: clean it up right away. Old oil, batteries and cleaning products are dangerous waste. They go to a special place, never in the normal bin or down the drain. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.garage.p: There is oil on the floor. I am cleaning it up.
gloss.c.garage.s: You need to look under a car. The car stands on a jack only. Your colleague says: "It is fine, just be quick." What do you do?
gloss.c.garage.o1: Wait until the car stands on the lift or on stands.
gloss.c.garage.o2: Go under it quickly, and keep your legs outside.
gloss.c.garage.o3: Go under it, and ask your colleague to hold the car.
gloss.c.garage.w: A jack can slip. A car is very heavy, and under it you cannot get away fast. Stands or a lift keep the car in its place.
gloss.c.carjob: Extra work? Ask the customer first
gloss.c.carjob.b: Do you find more problems than the work order says? Do not just fix them. The customer must agree to the extra work and the costs first. Your supervisor or the service desk calls the customer. A test drive is only with permission, and only with a valid driving licence. Write down what you did and which parts you used. General information. For your situation: ask your employer, the union or the Juridisch Loket.
gloss.c.carjob.p: I see another problem. Who calls the customer?
gloss.c.carjob.s: You change the oil of a car. You see that the brakes are bad too. The car must be ready in one hour. What do you do?
gloss.c.carjob.o1: Tell your supervisor, so they can call the customer.
gloss.c.carjob.o2: Fix the brakes too: the customer surely wants a safe car.
gloss.c.carjob.o3: Say nothing: the brakes are not on the work order.
gloss.c.carjob.w: The customer pays, so the customer decides. Without their OK, the garage may not just do extra work. Bad brakes are dangerous, so telling someone matters.
gloss.c.placement.b: In Entree you learn a lot at a company: your work placement (stage, or bpv). Before you start, you, the school and the company sign an agreement: the POK. At the company, your workplace trainer (praktijkopleider) helps you. At school, your placement coach (stagebegeleider) helps you. Sick? Call the company before your start time, and tell the school too. Rules differ per school: ask your placement coach.
gloss.c.placement.p: I only start when the placement agreement is signed.
gloss.c.placement.s: The company asks you to start tomorrow. The POK is not signed yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.placement.o1: Ask your placement coach to arrange the POK first.
gloss.c.placement.o2: Start tomorrow, and sign the POK when you have time.
gloss.c.placement.o3: Start, but do not tell the school about it yet.
gloss.c.placement.w: The POK says what you learn and who helps you. Without a signed POK, your placement may not count for your diploma. So you sign it before you start.
gloss.c.review: Ask for feedback, and for an example
gloss.c.review.b: At your placement, people tell you what goes well and what can be better: feedback. That is normal, and it helps you learn. You do not understand it? Ask for an example. Ask for feedback yourself too, for example once a week. Is something really wrong at your placement? First talk to your workplace trainer. Does that not help? Then go to your placement coach at school.
gloss.c.review.p: What went well, and what can be better?
gloss.c.review.s: Your workplace trainer says: "You must work more carefully." You do not know what they mean. What do you do?
gloss.c.review.o1: Ask for an example of what you must do differently.
gloss.c.review.o2: Say yes, and hope that you find out yourself.
gloss.c.review.o3: Work much slower from now on, so that nothing goes wrong.
gloss.c.review.w: With an example, you know what to change. Asking shows that you want to learn. Trainers like that.
gloss.c.council.b: In the Netherlands you choose who decides, by voting. The gemeenteraad decides about your town. The Tweede Kamer makes the laws for the whole country. With Dutch nationality, you may vote in every election, from 18. For the gemeenteraad, more people may vote: people from another EU country who live here, and people from outside the EU after 5 years of legal stay. The gemeente sends you a voting pass (stempas). Bring it with your ID. Not sure if you may vote? Ask the gemeente.
gloss.c.council.p: May I vote for the gemeenteraad?
gloss.c.council.s: You come from Morocco and have lived here legally for six years. You do not have Dutch nationality. There is an election for the gemeenteraad. What is true?
gloss.c.council.o1: You may vote for the gemeenteraad.
gloss.c.council.o2: You may vote for the Tweede Kamer too.
gloss.c.council.o3: You may not vote at all without a Dutch passport.
gloss.c.council.w: After 5 years of legal stay, you may vote for the gemeenteraad. For the Tweede Kamer, you need Dutch nationality.
gloss.c.police.b: From 14, you must show your ID when the police ask for it. So always carry it with you. Do you get a letter with a decision you do not agree with, for example from the gemeente or the UWV? Then you can object (bezwaar maken) in writing. Do it before the date in the letter. The police and the judge must treat everyone equally. Arrested? You may ask for a lawyer. The Juridisch Loket gives free advice.
gloss.c.police.p: I do not agree with this decision. I am objecting.
gloss.c.police.s: You get a letter from the gemeente. You do not agree with their decision. The letter says you have six weeks. What do you do?
gloss.c.police.o1: Write a letter to object, before the date.
gloss.c.police.o2: Call them once, and wait until they call you back.
gloss.c.police.o3: Wait: after six weeks, it stops by itself.
gloss.c.police.w: You object in writing, before the date in the letter. After that date, it is often too late. The Juridisch Loket can help you write it.
gloss.c.login.b: Your password and your DigiD are only for you. Do not give them to anyone, also not to your employer or a colleague. On a shared computer, always log out when you are done. Going away for a moment? Lock your screen. Forgot your password? Ask the IT department (ICT-afdeling) for a new one. Computer rules differ per company: ask the IT department what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.login.p: I am going away for a moment. I am locking my screen.
gloss.c.login.s: Your supervisor asks for your DigiD and password, to arrange your papers quickly. What do you do?
gloss.c.login.o1: Say no, and log in yourself while they help.
gloss.c.login.o2: Give it this one time, because it is your boss.
gloss.c.login.o3: Write it on a paper, so they can use it later.
gloss.c.login.w: With your DigiD, someone can see and change your tax, benefits and health papers. It is only for you. You can log in yourself and let someone help you.
gloss.c.phish: In a hurry, with a button? Do not click
gloss.c.phish.b: A fake e-mail (phishing) often looks real. It wants you to act fast: "Your account will be closed today!" Check the sender. Do not click on a link or open an attachment you did not expect. Go to the real website or app yourself. Did you click anyway? Change your password right away, and call the IT department. That is not a shame: the sooner they know, the better. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.phish.p: I clicked on a suspicious link.
gloss.c.phish.s: You clicked on a link in an e-mail and typed your password. Then you see that the e-mail was fake. What do you do?
gloss.c.phish.o1: Change your password, and call the IT department.
gloss.c.phish.o2: Delete the e-mail, so that nobody else clicks on it.
gloss.c.phish.o3: Wait a day to see if something goes wrong.
gloss.c.phish.w: With your password, someone else can get into the systems of your work. When you change it fast and tell the IT department, they can stop it in time.
gloss.c.mychoice.b: What are you good at? Think of work, school and home. Caring for family, a side job or volunteer work count too. What do you like, and what do you not like? Not sure what work fits you? Ask to join someone at work for a day (meeloopdag). Your coach at school can help you choose.
gloss.c.mychoice.p: I get on well with people. I help a lot at home.
gloss.c.mychoice.s: At school they ask: "What are you good at?" You never had a paid job. What do you say?
gloss.c.mychoice.o1: What you do well at home, like caring for others.
gloss.c.mychoice.o2: That you do not know yet, because you never had a job.
gloss.c.mychoice.o3: That you can do every kind of work, all of it.
gloss.c.mychoice.w: Skills from home count too. Caring, planning and helping are skills that employers need. Say what you did, with an example.
gloss.c.nextstep.b: With an Entree diploma, you may go on to level 2 of the mbo. A diploma at level 2 or higher is a basic qualification (startkwalificatie). It helps you to find work and to keep it. In the bbl you work at a company and go to school about one day a week. For that you need a job or a work-and-learn place (leerwerkbaan). Go to an open day, and talk to your coach at school.
gloss.c.nextstep.p: Can I go to level 2 after Entree?
gloss.c.nextstep.s: You have your Entree diploma. A company offers you a job without training. You also want to keep learning. What do you do?
gloss.c.nextstep.o1: Ask the company if a bbl place is possible.
gloss.c.nextstep.o2: Take the job, and stop learning for good.
gloss.c.nextstep.o3: Stay at home until a school calls you.
gloss.c.nextstep.w: With the bbl, you work and learn at the same time. You earn money, and you get a level 2 diploma. Many companies like this.
gloss.c.email: A short e-mail: who, what, when
gloss.c.email.b: An e-mail to work is short and polite. Start with a greeting, like "Beste Karin,". Then say what you want, and when. End with a greeting and your full name. Write a short subject, like "Vrij op vrijdag". Read your e-mail again before you send it.
gloss.c.email.p: Dear Karin, may I have Friday off? Regards, Ali Haddad
gloss.c.email.s: You want a day off next Friday. Which e-mail to your supervisor is best?
gloss.c.email.o1: "Beste Karin, mag ik vrijdag vrij? Groet, Ali Haddad"
gloss.c.email.o2: "Vrijdag ben ik er niet." (without a greeting or your name).
gloss.c.email.o3: A long e-mail about your week, with the question at the end.
gloss.c.email.w: A good e-mail has a greeting, one clear question and your name. Then your supervisor can answer quickly.
gloss.c.budget.b: When you get your pay, first pay the fixed costs: rent, insurance and your phone. Try to save a small amount every month, also 10 euros. Buy now, pay later is also a debt. Did you buy something online? Then you can usually change your mind within 14 days. Keep the receipt: you need it for the guarantee.
gloss.c.budget.p: I prefer to pay now. Then I have no debt.
gloss.c.budget.s: You get your pay today. You want new shoes, and your rent must still be paid. What do you do?
gloss.c.budget.o1: Pay the rent first, then see what is left.
gloss.c.budget.o2: Buy the shoes, and pay the rent later.
gloss.c.budget.o3: Buy the shoes with buy now, pay later.
gloss.c.budget.w: Rent, insurance and your phone come back every month. When you pay those first, you know what money is left. Then you do not get debts.
gloss.c.healthy.b: You work better and more safely when you sleep enough, also after a late shift. Eat breakfast, and drink water during the day. Move in your break, for example a short walk. Working under the influence of alcohol or drugs is dangerous, and most employers forbid it. Do you feel low for a long time, or can you not stop drinking or using? Talk to your huisarts. They can help, and they keep it secret.
gloss.c.healthy.p: I have felt low for a long time. Can I make an appointment?
gloss.c.healthy.s: You have a night shift tonight. A colleague offers you a pill to stay awake. What do you do?
gloss.c.healthy.o1: Say no, and sleep a few hours before your shift.
gloss.c.healthy.o2: Take half a pill, that is not dangerous.
gloss.c.healthy.o3: Take it, but tell nobody at work about it.
gloss.c.healthy.w: Pills from a colleague can be drugs. They can make you sick, or make you make mistakes at work. Sleep is the safe way to stay awake.
